name: colonies-02-parallel-multigen-perf
title: Parallel multi-generation colony — natural-division perf & Ray scaling
description:
Rerun the colony from one whole-cell agent, dividing naturally (no forced
same-tick division), keeping both daughters, as it doubles 1 → 2 → 4 → 8.
Track the per-cell compute hit (wall, RSS) generation-by-generation to resolve
colonies-01's open F-06 anomaly (RSS climbing ~5 MB/sim-s in long runs) and its
PASS-narrow caveat (only forced division was validated). Run the same growing
colony under the process-bigraph Ray protocol (sharded RayProtocol / actor
pool) to test whether process-level parallelism lifts the single-process
~13-cells GIL ceiling. Produce a compute-requirements profile seeding
colonies-03-hpc-deployment.

visualizations.name: colony-animation
visualizations.description:
A colony growing from ONE whole-cell agent by NATURAL division (no forcing):
each cell elongates as its dry mass accumulates toward the division threshold
(~one cell cycle ≈ 2400 ticks), then splits into two daughters that reset and
regrow — 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 6 cells over ~5300 ticks (subsampled 1 frame/40 ticks).
Fixed physics: jitter_per_second=1e-4 (the old 0.5 flung cells around the
frame) + coherent fg body mass + the viva-munk in-place shape update. Capsules
are cells; daughters are hue-shifted variants of their mother (phylogeny
coloring). Capped at gen 2 to stay under the F-04 native RAM ceiling.
Regenerate via
`python .../colonies-02-parallel-multigen-perf/sims/make_gif.py`.

visualizations.name: rss-vs-tick-by-ncells
visualizations.description:
Process RSS vs tick from a controlled staged run (N=1→2→4, force-divided for
timing; sims/mem_measure.py → runs/mem_measure.csv). The two memory factors
are visible in one figure: the step-up at each division = the per-cell
footprint, and the upward slope within each constant-N plateau = per-tick RSS
growth (annotated MB/tick). NOTE: this slope was measured on the macOS mini,
where it is dominated by allocator-arena churn; on Linux/glibc it is bounded
(0.017 MB/tick, 0.000 with malloc_trim). See F-03.

visualizations.name: footprint-and-leak-by-ncells
visualizations.description:
Left: per-cell footprint (GB/cell). Each colony cell is an independent full
baseline whole-cell composite that loads its own sim_data, so RAM scales ~1+
GB per cell (bounded, but the dominant cells-per-node limiter). Right: the
per-tick RSS-growth rate (within-plateau slope, MB/tick). Measured on the
macOS mini, where the slope is allocator-arena churn; Linux-bounded (F-03),
so not the cells-per-node limiter it appears here.

visualizations.name: memory-decomposition
visualizations.description:
RSS split into numpy-object bytes (gc-visible) vs native/C. numpy stays flat
within each plateau while native grows, so the growth is not a retained
Python/numpy object. The 2026-07-26 hunt (F-03) attributed it to the
elongation step (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%): ~0.2 MB/tick of truly
retained scipy LSODA work arrays plus macOS allocator-arena retention of
freed numpy buffers (invisible to tracemalloc). Linux-bounded. See
colonies-03 F-05 + issue #253.

purpose.question:
Starting from one whole-cell E. coli agent dividing naturally through 3-4
generations (1 → 2 → 4 → 8), does per-cell compute cost (wall + RSS) stay
flat, or drift as daughter EcoliWCM internal composites accumulate history?
And does running the growing colony under the process-bigraph Ray protocol
(one OS process per cell / sharded actor pool) lift the single-process GIL
ceiling colonies-01 measured (~13 cells/process at realtime)?
purpose.mechanism:
The `colony` composite (v2ecoli/composites/colony.py) wires N copies of
EcoliWCM (v2ecoli/bridge.py) into one pymunk 2D environment from viva-munk.
At division the bridge emits a structural update (_remove mother, _add two
daughter EcoliWCMs) hydrated natively by the engine (the colonies-01
daughter-hydration fix). Sequential runs walk all inner 55-process WCM steps
on one GIL-bound thread. The Ray protocol (process_bigraph/protocols/ray.py —
RayProtocol sharded actor pool via `ray:EcoliWCM` + Composite
parallel_processes=True) runs each cell's update in its own OS process, so
independent cells solve concurrently across cores.
purpose.expected_outcome:
(H1, drift) Per-cell wall drifts <=20% across gens 0-3; if >20%, the inner
composite is accumulating dead nodes / growing allocations (resolves F-06).
(H2, RSS) Per-cell RSS stays bounded once startup is amortized; the
~5 MB/sim-s climb is pre-division warmup, not an unbounded leak. (H3, Ray)
Under Ray, total wall stays sub-realtime well past the ~13-cell single-process
ceiling, with biology (masses, division timing) consistent vs the sequential
run modulo RNG.

build_tasks.motivation:
colony.gif shows excessive cell movement. Two coupled causes:
(1) colony.py passes jitter_per_second=0.5, ~5000x viva-munk's 1e-4
    schema default; jitter is a Gaussian impulse applied per substep
    (multibody.apply_jitter_force) and velocity change = impulse/mass.
(2) EcoliWCM emits dry_mass ~380 (fg, raw number) -> body.mass=380,
    but build_microbe's initial body is density=0.02 -> mass ~0.056.
    If the WCM mass does not actually land (or units are off), the
    effective body mass is tiny and the high jitter flings cells.
build_tasks.action:
5-tick diagnostic: print body.mass per cell each tick (does WCM
dry_mass reach the pymunk body?) and per-tick displacement. Decide
the fix: (a) lower jitter_per_second to the viva-munk default range,
and/or (b) correct the mass->pymunk coupling (scale dry_mass to a
consistent physics mass unit, or drive density from cell geometry).

build_tasks.motivation:
Run the growing colony under the updated process-bigraph Ray protocol.
Cells are `local:EcoliWCM` today (incl. daughters added by
_handle_division in bridge.py). To parallelize, both initial cells AND
dynamically-added daughters must use the Ray address.
build_tasks.action:
Wire EcoliWCM through RayProtocol: register_process_class("EcoliWCM", ..),
switch cell address to `ray:EcoliWCM`, build with parallel_processes=True,
and update bridge._handle_division so daughter specs inherit the Ray
address. Per-actor ParCa cache loading via register_type_provider so each
actor hydrates its own sim_data (relates to the parca-cache-contention
open question). Verify daughters hydrate as Ray actors, not local procs.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
colonies-01-hpc-readiness.gate_status == passed (satisfied) AND
per_cell_ms / per_cell_rss recorded as projection inputs.
pipeline_gate.blocks_until_resolved:
RESOLVED (2026-07-26). The prior block -- that the F-06 RSS climb might
be an unbounded leak OOMing before gen 3 -- was a macOS allocator-arena
artifact. On the Linux HPC target memory is bounded (F-03: 0.017 MB/tick
on glibc, 0.000 with malloc_trim), natural multi-generation division runs
unattended (F-01), and daughters hydrate under Ray (F-06). The
cells-per-node budget colonies-03 will validate is therefore trustworthy;
HPC deployment may proceed.

simulation_set.name: seq-1cell-4div
simulation_set.description:
Sequential (single-threaded) baseline. One cell, natural division,
~3 generations. Per-tick wall, per-cell wall, pymunk_step_ms, RSS,
live_cell_count, generation index recorded each tick. This is the
drift reference and the F-06 resolution run.

simulation_set.name: ray-1cell-4div
simulation_set.description:
Same natural-division colony under the process-bigraph Ray protocol
(ray:EcoliWCM, parallel_processes=True, sharded actor pool). Measures
whether per-cell wall stays flat AND whether total wall stays
sub-realtime past the single-process GIL ceiling as the colony grows.

simulation_set.name: ray-nsweep-static
simulation_set.description:
Optional confirmation: hold N static at {2,4,8,16} under Ray and
measure total wall vs N. Sequential crossed realtime at N~13; Ray
should push that ceiling out by ~n_cores. Short windows (60 ticks).

behavior_tests.name: natural-division-2-generations
behavior_tests.description:
One cell divides NATURALLY (no --force-divide) to 2, then both
daughters divide to 4 — all cells advancing on subsequent ticks.
Resolves colonies-01's PASS-narrow (forced-division-only) caveat.

behavior_tests.name: per-cell-wall-drift-within-20pct
behavior_tests.description:
Per-cell wall (ms/tick/cell) drifts <=20% across generations 0-3 of
the natural-division colony. Directly resolves F-06 for wall time.

behavior_tests.name: per-cell-rss-drift-bounded
behavior_tests.description:
Per-cell RSS is bounded on the Linux HPC target rather than climbing
unbounded. Reframed by the 2026-07-26 leak hunt (F-03): the scary mini
climb was macOS allocator-arena churn (Linux-bounded to 0.017 MB/tick on
glibc, 0.000 with malloc_trim); the only true retention is ~0.2 MB/tick of
scipy LSODA work arrays. Mechanism-validated on Linux, not a mini-measured
pass. Resolves F-06 for RAM.

behavior_tests.name: ray-lifts-gil-ceiling
behavior_tests.description:
Under the Ray protocol, total wall for the growing colony stays
sub-realtime past the sequential ~13-cell ceiling (target: scales
with cores), with division timing + masses consistent vs sequential.

behavior_tests.name: ray-biology-consistency
behavior_tests.description:
Ray and sequential runs produce the same colony trajectory (cell
count over time, per-cell mass at division) modulo RNG ordering.

conclusion:
This study delivers Part A enabling compute infrastructure for the colonies
investigation: correct natural multi-generation division (F-01), a flat
per-cell wall cost (~55-60 ms/tick/cell sequential, F-02; ~57 ms/tick/cell in
the merged 2026-07-26 remote re-run), Ray process-parallelism that lifts the
single-process GIL ceiling (~3.5x cells-per-core, F-04/F-06), and a now
characterised, Linux-bounded memory profile. It is not the scientific payload
(that is Part B: whether WCM single-cell phenotypes survive colony embedding +
division and match microfluidic-device data across the tier ladder).

The earlier "per-cell RSS leaks without bound, OOMs ~gen 3, so the 384/node
budget is untrustworthy" conclusion was WRONG and is retracted. The
2026-07-26 leak hunt localized the per-tick growth to the inner WCM's
elongation step (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%), decomposing into ~0.2 MB/tick
of truly retained scipy LSODA work arrays and a much larger macOS
allocator-arena retention of freed numpy buffers. Linux validation (colima
glibc) grew 0.017 MB/tick with no fix and 0.000 with periodic malloc_trim(0),
versus ~1.6 MB/tick on the macOS mini. So on the Linux HPC target memory is
bounded; the leak is a characterised, mitigated footnote (residual target:
the ~0.2 MB/tick LSODA arena via solver reuse or periodic trim), not the story.

Gate: unblocked. The block existed only because of the presumed unbounded
native leak; the corrected diagnosis (localized + Linux-bounded) removes it,
and the remaining behavior tests are satisfied by recorded data --
natural-division-2-generations (F-01), per-cell-wall-drift-within-20pct (F-02,
1.8% drift), ray-lifts-gil-ceiling (F-04), ray-biology-consistency (F-06).
per-cell-rss-drift-bounded is satisfied on the Linux target by
mechanism-validation (glibc container), not a mini-measured pass; the residual
scipy retention is noted honestly. HPC deployment (colonies-03) may proceed.

findings.statement:
One whole-cell agent divides naturally (no forced same-tick division)
through >=3 generations: 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 6 -> 8 -> 10 -> 12 -> 14 cells
(7 division events) in the sequential run, with all cells advancing on
subsequent ticks. Resolves the colonies-01 PASS-narrow caveat (which
validated FORCED division only). Daughter EcoliWCMs hydrate natively
via the bridge _remove/_add structural update.

expected.summary: one cell divides to 2 then both daughters to 4, all advancing.

findings.next_action: Natural multi-gen division is a usable substrate; memory is Linux-bounded (F-03), so it is HPC-ready enabling infrastructure.

findings.statement:
Per-cell EcoliWCM wall does not drift across generations. The cleanest
comparison (low-RSS static N-sweep, 60-tick windows): per-cell wall is
flat at 54-59 ms across N in {1,2,4,8,16} (65->54 ms, a slight decrease
as overhead amortizes). In the growing sequential run the 1-cell gen
(55.3 ms) vs 2-cell gen (56.3 ms/cell) differ by only +1.8%. Apparent
inflation to ~80 ms/cell at 14 cells is swap pressure (F-03) + O(N)
pymunk collision cost, not WCM-internal accumulation. Resolves F-06
for wall time: no per-cell wall drift.
findings.next_action: Use ~55-60 ms/tick/cell (sequential) as the per-cell wall projection input.

findings.statement:
CORRECTED by the 2026-07-26 leak hunt + Linux validation (supersedes the
earlier "unbounded native leak" reading recorded below). Per-process RSS
attribution on the mini localized the per-tick growth to the inner WCM's
polypeptide-elongation step (~82%) plus the mass-listener (~17%) -- it is
NOT an unbounded native leak. It decomposes into two parts: (1) a small
real retention of ~0.2 MB/tick (tracemalloc-visible), the scipy LSODA
integrator work arrays (rwork/iwork) held per solve_ivp(method="LSODA")
in the equilibrium / two-component / tRNA-charging ODEs -- ~0.6 GB over a
~3000-tick cell cycle, a small named optimization target (solver reuse /
method change / periodic trim); and (2) allocator ARENA retention -- the
scary ~1.4 MB/tick was the elongation step's large per-tick numpy working
arrays (buildSequences/polymerize, ~1.3 MB) which are freed but macOS does
not return to the OS, so mini RSS climbs (invisible to tracemalloc). Linux
validation (colima glibc container, faithful reproduction of both sources)
grew 0.017 MB/tick WITHOUT any fix and 0.000 with periodic malloc_trim(0),
versus ~1.6 MB/tick on the macOS mini. So on the Linux HPC target the
colony's memory is BOUNDED; the OOM / unbounded-leak framing below was
substantially a macOS measurement artifact. The macOS-mini figures in
`observed` (7.7 MB/sim-s, ~19 GB at first division, 27.5 GB peak, OOM at
tick 8161) are retained as the original mini measurements, now understood
as arena churn, not a Linux-relevant leak. Also corrected: an intermediate
"emitter is 94% of the leak" reading was a warm-process artifact and is
WRONG -- the growth is intrinsic to comp.run() (elongation), as above.

evidence.units: MB (macos_mini_* are macOS allocator-arena artifacts; linux_* are the HPC-target measurements)

expected.summary: per-cell RSS stabilizes after startup (the ~5 MB/sim-s climb is warmup).

findings.next_action:
No longer blocks colonies-03-hpc-deployment: memory is Linux-bounded
(0.017 MB/tick on glibc, 0.000 with malloc_trim). Residual optimization
target is the ~0.2 MB/tick scipy LSODA arena (solver reuse / periodic
trim); enable malloc_trim on the HPC target for headroom.

findings.statement:
The process-bigraph Ray protocol (ray:EcoliWCM, parallel_processes=True)
lifts the single-process GIL ceiling. Static N-sweep median wall (realtime
ratio): local scales linearly 65/118/237/466/865 ms (ratio 0.07->0.87)
for N=1/2/4/8/16, crossing realtime near N~18 (the colonies-01 ceiling).
Ray scales sub-linearly 54/59/81/115/245 ms (ratio 0.05->0.25): per-cell
wall drops 54->15 ms as cells solve concurrently across cores. At N=16
Ray is 3.5x faster and only 0.25 realtime, with headroom to ~50-60 cells
before realtime. Confirmed in the growing colony too: 2 cells cost the
same total wall (~59 ms) as 1 cell.

expected.summary: Ray total wall stays sub-realtime past the sequential ~13-cell ceiling.

findings.next_action:
CPU/GIL is no longer the ceiling under Ray (~3.5x sequential
cells-per-core). RAM is a bounded, budgetable overhead on Linux (F-03, F-05),
not a runaway per-generation leak.

findings.statement:
Under Ray the binding constraint flips from CPU/GIL to aggregate RAM,
and RAM is worse than sequential. The ~7.7 MB/sim-s per-cell leak (F-03)
is transport-independent: it moves into the actor process (one actor
reached ~19 GB by tick 2338, mirroring sequential). The Ray protocol also
pre-spawns a ~13-actor pool, each carrying a ~590 MB WCM baseline (~7.6 GB
fixed overhead). At just 2 live cells the two daughter actors were each
~10 GB and climbing (~34 GB distinct actor RSS), so a growing colony OOMs
the machine even faster than sequential. The main process stays flat
~0.7 GB (WCM offloaded). RSS sawtooths at division (mother actor returns
to pool).
Refined by the 2026-07-26 leak hunt (see F-03): the per-actor climb that
drove the ~19/34 GB figures is the same macOS allocator-arena artifact and
is Linux-bounded (0.017 MB/tick on glibc), so on the HPC target aggregate
actor RAM does NOT run away with generation age. The real, transport-
specific Ray cost is the FIXED pool baseline recorded here -- ~590 MB/idle
pool actor over a ~13-actor pool (~7.6 GB fixed) plus ~154 MB/cell steady
state (colonies-01 static sweep) -- not an unbounded per-cell leak. CPU/GIL
is the constraint Ray lifts (F-04); RAM is a bounded, budgetable overhead.

expected.summary: per-cell RSS bounded so Ray scales out across cores.

findings.next_action:
colonies-03 cells-per-node under Ray: budget the FIXED overhead
(~590 MB/idle-pool-actor + ~154 MB/cell steady state), not a per-generation
leak; memory is Linux-bounded (F-03) so Ray scale-out is viable. Optionally
enable malloc_trim on the target for headroom.

findings.statement:
Ray and sequential produce the same colony trajectory. First division
occurs at tick 2338 under both transports (exact, not just modulo RNG):
the EcoliWCM is deterministic given its seed and the transport does not
alter seeding, so division timing and per-cell mass are transport-
invariant. Per-cell wall under Ray at 2 cells is 29.7 ms (vs 59.8 ms at
1 cell): the two cells solve concurrently.

expected.summary: Ray and sequential agree on cell count over time + mass at division.

findings.next_action: Ray is a faithful drop-in for the biology; only its RAM profile differs (F-05).

findings.statement:
The colonies-01 excessive-cell-movement artifact has two coupled causes,
both confirmed by a 12-tick 2-cell diagnostic sweep over
(jitter_per_second, init_mass): (1) jitter_per_second=0.5 is ~5000x
viva-munk's 1e-4 default; (2) build_microbe's density(0.02)-seeded body
mass is ~0.04 (tiny), so jitter impulse/mass flings the cell. Legacy
(0.5, None): mean move 9-10 um/tick. Either fix alone tames it to
~0.13 um/tick; the chosen (1e-4, 200) fixes both motion and fg-unit
coherence (body mass ~200 fg). These are the run.py / study.yaml defaults.

expected.summary: lowering jitter and/or seeding a realistic fg mass collapses cell movement.

findings.next_action: Defaults (jitter=1e-4, init_mass=200) adopted in run.py and simulation_set.
